title: The Immortal Game
summary: The Immortal Game is remembered for Anderssen's willingness to give up material for a sustained attack on the Black king, with rooks, queen and knights all joining in. Watch how the evaluation swings: Black's early blunders hand White a winning attack, and Black's late errors turn a shaky position into a mating net. The critical moment is the sacrifice on g1 and the swift finish that follows.

title: The Evergreen Game
summary: The Evergreen Game is remembered for its sudden finish, in which Anderssen sacrifices his queen and a rook and ends with a bishop mate on e7. Black's queen raids on f5, h5 and f3 look greedy, and the engine shows how quickly the evaluation swings once White's pieces open lines against the king. Watch how the attack is built from loose pawns, open files and the bishop on d7.

title: The Opera Game
black: Duke Karl of Brunswick and Count Isouard
summary: The Opera Game, played by Paul Morphy in Paris in 1858, is remembered for its brilliant attack: White sacrifices material to open the d-file and the Black king never escapes the centre. Watch how Black's natural-looking moves, especially 9...b5 and 10...cxb5, hand White the open lines, and how the finish of 16.Qb8+ and 17.Rd8# ends the game on the back rank.

title: Rubinstein's Immortal
summary: Rubinstein's Immortal is remembered for a short, sharp sacrifice sequence in which Black gives up a rook to open White's king and then finishes with a bishop check and a mating net. The evaluation barely moves for 30 plies, so the lesson is in the slow buildup and in White's 19.e5 blunder, which handed Black a winning attack. Watch how Black's rooks and bishops are aimed at the king on h1 long before the sacrifices begin.

title: Reti vs Tartakower
summary: Reti's win against Tartakower is remembered for its short, sharp finish: a queen sacrifice on d8 and a bishop mate after Black's 8...Nxe4 blunder turned a level position into mate in three. Watch how White's open d-file and the king's exposure on c7 combine, and how Black's early queen check cost time.

title: Lasker vs Thomas: The King Hunt
summary: Lasker's attack is remembered because a quiet kingside position collapsed into a king hunt in about ten moves, with the king marched up the board by checks. The decisive turn came when Black's 10...Qe7 allowed a forced attack that the engine rated as mate. Watch how each check removes one of the king's escape squares.

title: The Game of the Century
summary: Remembered as the game in which the 13-year-old Fischer (16 at the time, though many accounts give his age as 13) sacrificed material to shatter White's king, which is why it is nicknamed the Game of the Century. The turning point came with 11.Bg5, after which the engine's evaluation swung sharply to Black and never recovered. Watch how Black keeps tempo on the queen, wins pawns with each knight check, and finishes with a rook mate on c2.

title: Polugaevsky vs Nezhmetdinov
summary: This game is remembered for Black's relentless pawn storm and the king hunt that followed White's king march into the centre. Watch how Black keeps the initiative with the f- and g-pawns, and how the decisive phase grows out of White's errors at moves 11, 20 and 27.

title: Fischer vs Spassky, Game 6
summary: Game 6 of the 1972 World Championship match in Reykjavik is widely remembered as a turning point, with Fischer's win ending in a kingside attack after a quiet opening. Watch how the position stays level until Black's 20...d4 gives White a clear space advantage, and how the f-pawn and rook lift decide the game.

title: Deep Blue vs Kasparov, Game 6
summary: Game 6 is remembered as the game where Kasparov resigned after 19.c4, with Deep Blue's attack on the uncastled king and the bishop sacrifice on f5 deciding the result. Watch how the engine's evaluation climbs after the early inaccuracy at 7...h6, and how each sacrifice opens lines towards Black's king.

title: Kasparov's Immortal
summary: Kasparov's win over Topalov at Wijk aan Zee in 1999 is remembered for its sacrificial attack, which the title nickname Immortal reflects, with a rook given up on d4 and the king hunted across the board. The turning points come after 24...cxd4, when the attack gathers force, and in the final phase, where Black's king walks into danger. Watch how each check opens a new line and how Black's king becomes the target.

title: Anand vs Carlsen, Game 9
summary: This game is remembered for the late promotion trick: Carlsen's pawn reached b1 with check and Anand's 28.Nf1 allowed a decisive pin. Watch how a double-edged position around the b-pawn and the blocked kingside decided everything in the last few moves.
